chunks: About a man who takes a loan from another man and gives him collateral, whether a servant, vessels, or clothes. Then he needs something from his belongings, so he asks his permission regarding it, and he permits him.
He said: "If he gives it willingly, then there is no harm."
I said: "Those with us narrate that every loan that draws a benefit is invalid."
So he said: "Is not the best loan that which brings a benefit?"

key_terms.الرَّهْنَ: collateral or pledged property held as security
key_terms.طَابَتْ نَفْسُهُ: he gave consent willingly and with a content heart
key_terms.قَرْضًا: a loan extended between two parties
key_terms.مَنْفَعَةً: a benefit or gain arising in the transaction

ai.seo_question: Is every loan that brings some benefit considered invalid in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling related to loans and pledged collateral. It indicates that if the owner of the collateral willingly permits use of it, there is no harm, and it clarifies that not every benefit associated with a loan is invalid in an absolute sense.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked him about a man who borrows a loan from another man and gives him collateral, either a servant, a vessel, or clothing.
Later, the borrower needs something from his belongings and seeks permission from the lender, who grants it.
Imam (as) said: "If the lender willingly allows it, then there is no harm."
I said: "Those among us narrate that any loan that brings benefit is invalid."
Imam (as) replied: "Isn't the best loan the one that brings benefit?"
